scriptFirst.spokenScript:
Three clubs. Two hands. Don't worry about the third club. Worry if you see me catch all three.

Last week a safety inspector came to watch. Waited till I had a good rhythm, pointed at the red one.

"What's that one for?"
"Juggling."
"Your hands are full."
"Exactly."
"Then it's surplus."

He made me stop. Took the red club away. Locked it in a drawer for public safety.

With two clubs, one hand is always free. No surprises. No risk. I did it for eleven minutes. The inspector wrote "demonstration successful." One child began stacking chairs. Frankly, it had better suspense.

I asked for the red club back.
"First prove you can manage three."
"I was."
"Then why did you stop?"

I pointed at the drawer.
"Don't change the subject."

Yesterday the lab returned the red one. No defects. Now he wants me to submit the other two so they can test how the three interact.

I told him the interaction's at eight on Friday.

Front row. He can stop it himself.
scriptFirst.stylePrompt: Rapid dry spoken English stand-up, strictly speech NOT singing. Close-miked adult clown voice with precise cynical timing. Sparse rockabilly trio: walking upright bass, light brushed snare, short hollow-body guitar stabs ONLY after actual reversals; drop to near silence for inspector exchanges and the final callback. No chorus, canned laughs, generic metaphors, slogan ending or narration of stage directions. One clean stop. Voice dominant over live band.
